newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks start lower, brush off Fin One slide.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks start lower, brush off Fin One slide.

text.p: Thai stocks opened lower on Friday as shares of troubled finance firm Finance One Plc FIN.BK opened at six baht in heavy early trade.
The SET Index had fallen 1.29 points or 0.23 percent to 556.88 by 0309 GMT. The SET 50 fell 0.13 point or 0.32 percent to 40.17. Turnover was 218 million baht.
But early losses were less than some had feared, with investors using predictions of a bad day for the market to accumulate blue chips on expectations of a technical rebound next week, traders said.
The market had rebounded by 0329 GMT, with the SET Index up 1.21 points at 559.38. Tunrover was 542 million baht.

"I think with this (the Finance One resumption) out of the way, people think all the bad news is out in the market and have come to buy other stocks on expectations of a rebound next week," said a trader at the Multi Credit Corporation.
Traders said most sell orders in Finance One were from foreigners and retailers who were forced to sell after buying the stock on credit earlier this year.
Traders said they suspected retailers forced to sell out of Finance One were using the cash to buy into other stocks.
Local speculators, encouraged by government pledges to support the firm, were believed to be the biggest buyers of Finance One shares, traders said.

Finance One, allowed a virtual free float, was trading at 7.20 baht by 0336 GMT. The 16.55 baht fall since the stock last traded in February knocked the finance sector 4.41 percent but most other key market sectors were up.
Krung Thai Bank Plc added 1.25 baht to 29.50 and Bangkok Bank Plc was up two baht to 148.
